findingDetails.title: Phase-child budget exemption claim contradicts budgetApplies(); nested phase parents and phase-level children are measured
findingDetails.evidence: budget-and-handoff.md:33 says 'Phase children are exempt from the cap, so their packet report has packet_budget=unknown.' goal-slice.cjs:380-382 reads: function budgetApplies(packetAbsolute) { return !isPhaseChild(packetAbsolute) || isPhaseParentFolder(packetAbsolute) || declaresPhaseLevel(packetAbsolute); } and its own comment (goal-slice.cjs ~292-296) says 'no budget applies to it unless it is itself a phase parent' and 'The validator budgets every folder it resolves to the phase level, even one nested inside another packet, and exempts only the other phase children.' The same blanket exemption appears at SKILL.md:108, goal-phase-child-template.md:25, sk-create-goal/README.md:92, goal-set-string-playbook.md:65, spec-kit-docs.json:26 and speckit-plan/implement/complete.yaml.
findingDetails.impact: For a phase child that is itself a phase parent or declares the phase level, goal.cjs packet applies the 4,000 budget and reports ok/over while every cited surface promises exemption and packet_budget=unknown. A doc-faithful author never trims such a goal; the send rule (budget-and-handoff.md:54) then refuses the only send path, and check-goal.cjs passes the file (see R1-P2-002), so nothing surfaces the problem at authoring time.
findingDetails.fix: Replace the first sentence of budget-and-handoff.md:33 with: 'A phase child is exempt from the cap only when it is not itself a phase parent and its spec.md does not declare the phase level; those are measured like any parent and report ok or over. An exempt child's packet report has packet_budget=unknown.' Mirror the same boundary in SKILL.md:108, goal-phase-child-template.md:25, sk-create-goal/README.md:92, goal-set-string-playbook.md:65 and the three speckit budget strings.
findingDetails.claim: Phase-child goals are exempt from the 4,000-character durable budget and their packet report always shows packet_budget=unknown.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched for a guarantee that no phase child can itself be a phase parent or declare a phase level; goal-slice.cjs:292-296 and the mirrored validator rule state the opposite explicitly ('budgets every folder it resolves to the phase level, even one nested inside another packet'). Also checked whether budgetApplies() short-circuits before the phase-parent test; it does not.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The surfaces use 'phase children' to mean only pure leaf children, with nested parents covered by their 'phase parent' clause; under that reading the sentences are shorthand rather than false. Rejected because the sentences assert the packet-report state ('has packet_budget=unknown'), which is observably wrong for a nested parent, and the child template states the exemption absolutely.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if the packet structure rules forbid any phase child from carrying its own phase children and from declaring a phase level (i.e. the branch in budgetApplies() is unreachable in this repository).

findingDetails.title: check-goal.cjs parent-budget check skips every phase child, diverging from goal.cjs on nested phase parents
findingDetails.evidence: check-goal.cjs:339: 'if (context.isPhaseChild) return [];' where isPhaseChildFolder (check-goal.cjs:76) is only 'parent directory contains spec.md'. goal-slice.cjs:380-382 additionally budgets a phase child when isPhaseParentFolder() or declaresPhaseLevel() holds. Same packet therefore yields check-goal 'parent-budget PASS' and goal.cjs packet_budget=over.
findingDetails.impact: The checker SKILL.md:110 tells an author to run and trust reports a clean budget for a nested parent that the packet report and the validator reject. The two tools the docs treat as interchangeable measurements (budget-and-handoff.md:66) disagree on applicability, so an over-budget nested parent survives the authoring gate.
findingDetails.fix: In evaluateParentBudget, replace 'if (context.isPhaseChild) return [];' with the same three-condition test goal-slice.cjs budgetApplies() uses: skip only when the packet is a phase child AND not a phase parent folder AND does not declare the phase level.

findingDetails.title: goal.cjs routes unrecognized tokens (including flags like --help) into the set action, and FAIL exits 0
findingDetails.evidence: goal.cjs:388 'const normalizedAction = core.ACTIONS.includes(action) ? action : \'set\';' and goal.cjs:426-431 default branch calls runSet(parsedScope.argv, ...). Observed: node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs --help prints 'STATUS=FAIL ACTION=set ERROR="Session identity is required" code=MISSING_SESSION_ID'. printFail() writes no exit code and main() sets none, so every failure exits 0.
findingDetails.impact: With a live session identity, a mistyped action or a help request silently replaces the session objective with the raw token text. Scripts cannot detect failure from the exit status. This also weakens SKILL.md:158, which introduces goal.cjs only as a printer of slices 'without binding a session' while the same binary mutates session state on bare text.
findingDetails.fix: In the default branch, refuse tokens that start with '-' with an UNKNOWN_ACTION failure instead of falling through to set, consider requiring an explicit 'set' for objective replacement, and set process.exitCode=1 inside printFail().

findingDetails.title: Presentation contract renders the /4000 measurement for exempt children and its handoff wording omits the packet_budget=ok send gate
findingDetails.evidence: create-goal-presentation.txt:108 renders 'Measured : durable {chars}/4000 chars packet_budget={state}' for every operation including child goals whose state is unknown; lines 111 and 127 say 'set or resend it' and 'Give the printed chat slice to your runtime\'s goal hook to set or resend the objective' with no packet_budget=ok condition. The canonical rule at budget-and-handoff.md:54 sends the chat_slice 'only when the same report shows packet_budget=ok'.
findingDetails.impact: The operator-facing surface is the one place the send gate could be restated at handoff time; without it the workflow can render a slice alongside packet_budget=over or unknown (over-budget escalation path, child operations) and the wording invites handing it over anyway, and a child measurement displayed against a 4000 denominator misstates the cap.
findingDetails.fix: At presentation line 108 render the denominator only when the report measures the packet (e.g. 'durable {chars} chars packet_budget={state}'), and append to lines 111 and 127: 'send it only when the report shows packet_budget=ok; cut the file first when it is over.'

findingDetails.title: budget-and-handoff.md Devin row cites goal-plugin line 170, which documents the shared CLI, not Devin wiring
findingDetails.evidence: Row cites '(goal plugin, lines 158 and 170)'. goal-plugin.md:158 is the Devin row of the support matrix; goal-plugin.md:170 is the shared-CLI paragraph ('The shared CLI keeps the base OpenCode action envelope and adds bind, unbind, ...'), which says nothing about Devin. The evidence for 'no Devin prompt-command surface' is line 158 and the command-surface table at 162-168, which lists OpenCode, Cursor and Pi only.
findingDetails.impact: One of the two cited lines does not support the claim it is offered for, so a reader verifying the runtime matrix lands on unrelated text. Low impact; the claim itself is supported by line 158.
findingDetails.fix: Change 'goal plugin, lines 158 and 170' to 'goal plugin, lines 158 and 162 to 168' in budget-and-handoff.md:87.
